decisions.quote:
According to Hofstede’s (1980, 1997)
typology, the Arab countries, to which Jordan belongs, were classified as having high power distance (80), high
uncertainty avoidance (68), a collectivist culture (91 on Individualism), and a masculine culture (53).
The aim of the study is to update the Hofstede cultural value dimensions. We argue that scores obtained by Hofstede in
his previous studies conducted in Arab countries and then findings generalized to Jordanian culture is not scientifically
valid. This study replicates Hofstede’s study with data obtained from students studying for their master degrees in
different universities in Jordan. To operationalize culture, Hofstede (1980) have used matched samples to eliminate
the effect of other factors. This study replicates Hofstede’s study in the same way; using a matched sample on as many
characteristics as possible (age and education).
decisions.location: Section 4 (Replication of Hofstede’s Cultural Dimensions in Jordan), p. 75, lines 244-252
decisions.reason: The paper explicitly re-tests the original IBM cross-cultural study and Arab-country cultural dimension scores attributed in-text to Hofstede (1980) (and reiterated in later book editions such as 1991, 1997, and 2005). Because the authors cite Hofstede (1980) repeatedly in-text (with author name and initial 'Hofstede, G.' established in the reference list) but omit the 1980 work from the reference list, the codebook requires recording the cited author and year ('Hofstede, G.', '1980') and leaving title and doi empty rather than supplying external metadata from memory. The shipped row erroneously assigns year_o '1999' (which never appears for Hofstede in the paper) and a title not printed in the primary text.

decisions.quote:
In conclusion we argue that Hofstede’s (1980, 1991, 2005) assumption that people who grow up in the same place will
share similar views about life does not apply to his findings about Arab cultures and thus his generalization made to
Jordanian culture is not validated.
decisions.reason: Although the Jordanian sample yielded scores similar to Hofstede's Arab-country scores on two dimensions (Masculinity: 51 vs. 53; Individualism: 27.2/27.7 vs. 38) and different scores on two dimensions (Power Distance: 7.75 vs. 80; Uncertainty Avoidance: 110 vs. 68), the authors state an explicit overall verdict in the Abstract and Conclusion that Hofstede's generalization of his Arab-country findings to Jordanian culture is 'not scientifically valid' and 'not validated'. Under Codebook Step 3 Rule 1, an explicit overall verdict on the replication as a whole governs over mixed individual comparisons.

decisions.quote:
This study replicates Hofstede’s
study with data obtained from students studying for their master degrees in different universities in Jordan.
decisions.reason: The study collects new primary survey data from 795 master's students across universities in Jordan using the VSM 94 questionnaire to re-test whether Hofstede's (1980) published cultural dimension findings for Arab countries hold in Jordan. Both shipped and blind coding rightly classify the record as a replication.
